items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: I have a production company with my partner in life, Jewel Kinch-Thomas, called G&J Productions

ctx.x: But you have economic realities that you’re dealing with — the clubs and all that stuff. So that must be a little awkward at times.

Yeah, it is. It is. I’ve been in a position where my production company — I have a production company with my partner in life, Jewel Kinch-Thomas, called G&J Productions, and we have produced any number of places: the Wainwright House in Rye, New York; Aaron Davis Hall in Harlem; Ginny’s Supper Club, which is below the Red Rooster in Harlem; Mist, Harlem on 116th between Lenox and Fifth, we did a jazz Sunday brunch there; any number of other places — Friar’s Club also. And so we’ve been in a position where we’ve…
sometimes that’s just what it comes down to. Yeah, so I mean yeah, you’re right. Sometimes it does hurt.
